remediationRecommendation.error: Instance termination due to critical errors
remediationRecommendation.cause: Oracle database instances underwent emergency shutdown due to critical errors that compromised database integrity. The termination was initiated by various Oracle background processes (CKPT, USER processes) when they encountered unrecoverable errors such as control file corruption, I/O failures, or other system-level issues. This represents the final stage of error escalation where Oracle determines the instance cannot safely continue operation.
remediation: Review Oracle diagnostic dumps and incident files for root cause analysis
Check system state dump files in $ORACLE_BASE/diag/rdbms/ordbsdl/ordbsdl/trace/
Verify storage subsystem health and connectivity to FSx for NetApp ONTAP
Restart Oracle instance after resolving underlying storage/network issues
Implement Oracle High Availability solutions (RAC, Data Guard) to prevent single points of failure
Enable automatic diagnostic repository (ADR) for better incident tracking
Configure Oracle Enterprise Manager or CloudWatch for proactive monitoring
Review and tune Oracle parameters related to error handling and recovery
Establish regular backup and recovery testing procedures

remediationRecommendation.error: Empty temporary tablespace after database creation
remediationRecommendation.cause: Temporary tablespace 'TEMP' was created without any tempfiles during database creation or restoration process. This commonly occurs when using backup control files or when the CREATE DATABASE command doesn't specify a default temporary tablespace. While not immediately critical, this can impact sort operations, temporary table creation, and overall database performance.
remediation: Add tempfile to TEMP tablespace: ALTER TABLESPACE TEMP ADD TEMPFILE '/mnt/oradata/ORDBSDL/temp01.dbf' SIZE 1G AUTOEXTEND ON
Verify temporary tablespace is set as default: ALTER DATABASE DEFAULT TEMPORARY TABLESPACE TEMP
Check available space in FSx for NetApp ONTAP volume before creating tempfiles
Monitor temporary tablespace usage and configure appropriate autoextend settings
Consider creating multiple tempfiles for better I/O distribution
remediationRecommendation.context: 2025-02-20T04:37:33.886013+00:00 Empty temporary tablespace TEMP detected after database creation. Recommendation provided to add tempfiles using ALTER TABLESPACE command.

remediationRecommendation.cause: Files exist in the db_recovery_file_dest location that are not registered in Oracle's recovery catalog. Verify db_recovery_file_dest parameter setting: SHOW PARAMETER db_recovery_file_dest

Configure RMAN retention policy appropriately for your backup strategy
remediationRecommendation.context: 2025-02-20T04:37:33.886013+00:00 Files exist in db_recovery_file_dest that are unknown to database. Caused by backup controlfile restoration or recovery area configuration changes.

remediationRecommendation.cause: Oracle Advanced Queuing (AQ) is not properly configured with AQ_TM_PROCESSES set to 0 and no enabled queues. This disables the AQ time manager and can impact applications that rely on message queuing functionality. While not critical for basic database operations, it may affect specific application features that use Oracle's messaging capabilities.
remediation: Configure AQ time manager: ALTER SYSTEM SET AQ_TM_PROCESSES=1
Enable queues if needed by applications: BEGIN DBMS_AQADM.START_QUEUE('queue_name'); END;
Review application requirements for Advanced Queuing functionality
Monitor queue performance if AQ is enabled for production use
Document AQ configuration requirements for future database deployments

remediationRecommendation.cause: Oracle detected a deadlock situation where two or more transactions were waiting for each other to release locks, creating a circular dependency. This is typically caused by applications accessing resources in different orders or inefficient SQL design. While Oracle automatically resolves deadlocks by rolling back one transaction, frequent deadlocks can indicate application design issues.
remediation: Review deadlock trace file for detailed analysis: /u01/app/oracle/diag/rdbms/ordbsdl/ordbsdl/trace/ordbsdl_ora_1182122.trc
Analyze application code to ensure consistent resource ordering
Implement proper exception handling for deadlock scenarios in applications

Use appropriate locking strategies (SELECT FOR UPDATE with NOWAIT)
Monitor deadlock frequency using AWR reports
Review and optimize SQL statements causing high contention
